name: Lexicon of the Dead Hand
description: A scribe's glossary of the script used before the cataclysm, annotated in three hands.
benefit: Lets the reader make sense of inscriptions written before the cataclysm.
cost: Reading from it takes a full rest, and a reader who cannot put it down loses a day to it.

name: Periplus of the Drowned Coast
description: A pilot's coastal chart, annotated by someone who survived the flood and was ashamed of it.
benefit: Marks every wreck and drowned polis on the coast.
cost: Its depths are decades out of date; a chart reader who trusts it over the lead is wrecked on its errors.

name: The Surveyors' Fair Copy
description: A clean map of the region, the one the Surveyors keep for themselves.
benefit: Reveals the points of interest within a day's walk of each settlement.
cost: The Surveyors know who holds it and lean on the bearer for a favour that will not wait.

name: The Harbourmaster's Tally
description: A fortnight of entries: ship, cargo, tonnage, and which clerk was paid to forget.
benefit: Shows every route that is running and what it pays, so trade can be timed.
cost: The ledger is evidence. Anyone caught carrying it is treated as a witness and watched.

name: The Satrap's Letter of Passage
description: Sealed vellum with a foreign name on it, signed by a man who has never seen the bearer.
benefit: Passes every checkpoint held by the occupying power without a fee or a search.
cost: Every resistance cell treats the bearer as a collaborator until proven otherwise.

name: The Warded Key Ring
description: Forty keys, none labelled, each cut to a lock that may or may not still exist.
benefit: Opens simple and complex locks alike, however well warded.
cost: A set that has opened a vault is known; the vault's owners will come looking.

name: The Oracle's Last Reply
description: A sentence spoken once, two hundred years ago, and recorded by a tired priest.
benefit: Tells the reader which of the world's dead sanctuaries still holds anything.
cost: Read aloud, it can be heard by anyone nearby, and the priesthoods who hear it close ranks.

name: Forecast of the Conqueror
description: A prophecy written down by three witnesses who disagreed about only the dates.
benefit: Reveals where the Foretold will be at the end of each week.
cost: Knowing the schedule fixes it: the bearer is held to blame for a march they could not stop.

name: Ariadne's Unfinished Thread
description: A ball of red thread with a map worked into its length, one knot per corridor.
benefit: Marks the way through any maze, tunnel or dungeon and back out again.
cost: It is unwound as used, one length per entry, and cannot be rewound.

name: Formulary of Purifications
description: A temple scribe's record of who was cleansed, with what, and what the cleansing cost them.
benefit: Names the remedy for any pollution the Miasma has spread through a place.
cost: Several remedies require the death of something innocent, and the book is honest about which.

name: Roll of the Unburied
description: A list of names, a place, and a date, for every body not yet laid to rest.
benefit: Marks every grave that still needs rites and which rites it needs.
cost: Most of the names are people the bearer will meet alive first, and the roll does not say which.

name: Tiresias's Confession
description: A single true statement, offered freely to whoever sits long enough to hear it.
benefit: Answers one question about the world, honestly and in full.
cost: It must be asked the day it is given, and the answer cannot be unheard.
